Generate H3 spatial bins

Source: R/space_bins.R
space_bins.Rd

A function to generate spatial hexagonal equal-area grid cells (i.e. bins) using the H3 discrete global grid system. These can then be used in bin_space() to assign fossil occurrences (or localities) to spatial bins.

Usage

space_bins(resolution, spacing, area)

Arguments

resolution

numeric. The desired H3 resolution. Must be a whole number between 0 and 15. Cannot be used if spacing or area is used.

spacing

numeric. The desired spacing between the centre of adjacent cells. This value should be provided in kilometres. Cannot be used if resolution or area is used.

area

numeric. The desired area of each cell. This value should be provided in square kilometres. Cannot be used if resolution or spacing is used.

Value

An object of class palaeoverse_space_bins. This object can be passed to the bins argument in bin_space() to assign occurrences (or any set of coordinates) to these bins. Under the hood, this is an sfc_POLYGON with CRS EPSG:4326 (WGS 1984). This object has an attribute h3_resolution that is currently used internally by bin_space() to name columns automatically, but may change in future releases.

Details

The H3 discrete global grid system uses fixed resolutions, which can be directly set by passing an H3 resolution level (0-15) to resolution. Alternatively, resolution can be inferred from a target spacing or area. spacing is defined as the distance between the centroids of adjacent cells; the function compares the input spacing to the average centroid distance at each H3 resolution and selects the closest match. Likewise, a target area is compared to the average cell area at each resolution, and the nearest resolution is used.

See also

Examples

space_bins(resolution = 1)
#> ℹ H3 resolution: 1
#> ℹ Average spacing between adjacent cells: 725.17 km.
#> ℹ Average cell area: 609,788.4 sq. km.
#> Geometry set for 842 features 
#> Geometry type: eoverse_space_bins
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -179.7613 ymin: -87.80824 xmax: 179.9534 ymax: 87.82362
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#> First 5 geometries:
#> POLYGON ((40.0114 75.01232, 55.65377 76.66744, ...
#> POLYGON ((13.88006 80.34595, 33.23853 83.59755,...
#> POLYGON ((67.04817 73.26747, 82.21912 72.97478,...
#> POLYGON ((61.13368 80.94452, 89.55466 80.74027,...
#> POLYGON ((31.83128 68.92996, 41.0975 70.96472, ...
